name: Elihu
description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: The three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes, and Elihu's wrath was kindled because Job justified himself rather than God. Job said he was not weak like Adam. That was his flaw: he was over-righteous.

These three men ceased to answer Job because he was righteous in his own eyes. Then the wrath of Elihu the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the kindred of Ram, was kindled against Job because he justified himself rather than God.

Elihu recognized who his elders were. He did not talk out of turn or try to make himself equal to them. He sat back like a young man should, let the older men discuss what they needed to discuss, and came afterward once they were finished.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man

points: Elihu answered and said he is young and they are very old, so he was afraid and durst not show his opinion. He said days should speak and multitude of years should teach wisdom.

note.label: Job 32: The Wrath Of Elihu The Young Man
